summary: Release engineering is half-mature: there is a real tag-driven release workflow, a genuinely good version-scoped artifact validator with its own unit tests, a multi-version CI matrix with an integration smoke test, and version-consistency guard tests. But the actual published artifact is broken (the wheel omits the root `setup.py` wizard module that `latticeai/server_app.py` imports at top level, and CI only ever tests `pip install -e .` from the repo root, so this is never caught), there is zero Python lint/typecheck tooling (only py_compile syntax checks), all dependencies are completely unpinned, and the working directory is a 2.9GB junk drawer (31 ltcai-*.tgz tarballs, two virtualenvs, an extracted release dir, logs, .env) with a 15MB .pptx tracked in git history and HEAD.
strengths: scripts/validate_release_artifacts.py is high quality: validates exact version-named wheel/sdist/VSIX, inspects VSIX zip for compiled entrypoint and internal version match, warns loudly against dist/* glob uploads mixing stale versions — and it is itself unit-tested (tests/unit/test_release_artifacts.py).

tests/unit/test_version_consistency.py enforces one canonical version (latticeai.core.workspace_os.WORKSPACE_OS_VERSION) against pyproject.toml, package.json, both package-lock.json files, vscode-extension/package.json, static/v3/asset-manifest.json, and even bans hard-coded version literals in settings.js (must read /health).
scripts/build_vsix.mjs fails on root-vs-extension version drift, installs the toolchain on clean clones, and verifies out/extension.js exists before packaging — documented rationale in the header.

.github/workflows/ci.yml is real CI: Python 3.11+3.12 matrix, discovery-based syntax gate (scripts/check_python.py auto-includes new modules so the gate can never fall behind), unit tests, then a live-uvicorn integration smoke job with /health wait and log dump on failure, then build + twine check with version extracted from pyproject.

.github/workflows/release.yml is tag-driven and intentionally builds/validates only — publishing is manual, so pushing a tag can never accidentally publish to PyPI/npm/Marketplace (documented in the file header).

.gitignore correctly excludes secrets and runtime state: .env, *.tgz, dist/, *.log, chat_history.json, telegram_chats.json, users.json, sessions.json, agent_workspace/, both venvs; verified via git log that .env and chat_history.json were never committed.
Test tree is cleanly separated: tests/unit (49 files, 455 passing), tests/integration (live-server), tests/visual (Playwright specs + daily-cron visual.yml workflow).
tests/unit/test_static_release_hygiene.py guards static-serving regressions (favicon route, no stale ?v= query-version asset references — hashed manifest enforced).

problems.title: Published wheel is broken: root setup.py module is imported but never packaged
problems.detail: latticeai/server_app.py:149 and latticeai/api/setup.py:19 do top-level `from setup import get_recommendations, scan_environment` — `setup` here is the 52KB Setup Wizard application module at repo root. But pyproject.toml [tool.setuptools] py-modules (lines 65-78) omits "setup", and inspecting dist/ltcai-3.6.0-py3-none-any.whl confirms no top-level setup.py is installed (only auto_setup.py, server.py, knowledge_graph.py, etc.). Any `pip install ltcai` followed by running the LTCAI console script will crash with ImportError before the server starts. CI masks this because ci.yml installs with `pip install -e .` from the repo root where setup.py resolves via sys.path, and release.yml only runs `pip install -r requirements.txt` + tests from checkout. Neither workflow ever installs the built wheel into a clean env and imports it. The shipped artifact for at least v3.6.0 is dead on arrival — the strongest possible signal that release validation checks names, not function.

problems.title: setup.py is application code, not a packaging script (name collision with setuptools)
problems.detail: The repo-root setup.py is the "Smart Setup Wizard — Environment Scanner, Recommender & Auto-Installer" (subprocess helpers, SSE streaming, download URLs) — not a setuptools script. setuptools' build backend executes setup.py when present, so application code runs during every `python -m build` / `pip install -e .`. This is both the root cause of the packaging omission above and a standing hazard: any future top-level statement with side effects in this file executes inside the build sandbox. It must be renamed (e.g. latticeai/services/setup_wizard.py) for v4.

problems.title: No Python lint or typecheck whatsoever; JS 'lint' is only a syntax check
problems.detail: There is no ruff/flake8/mypy/pyright config anywhere — no [tool.ruff]/[tool.mypy] in pyproject.toml, no setup.cfg, no pytest.ini (pytest runs with zero configuration, including no asyncio mode setting despite pytest-asyncio being installed in CI). The only Python gate is scripts/check_python.py, which is py_compile — it catches syntax errors only. The npm `lint` script (package.json line 24) is a chain of `node --check` calls plus scripts/lint_v3.mjs which is also just `node --check` per file: no ESLint, no Prettier, no semantic linting at all for ~40 frontend JS modules. `typecheck` (line 26) only compiles the vscode-extension TypeScript. For a codebase with a 204KB knowledge_graph.py single module, this is a major quality gap for v4.

problems.title: Wheel pollutes site-packages with generic top-level modules and a 'tools' package
problems.detail: pyproject.toml installs 12 top-level py-modules with collision-prone generic names (server, kg_schema, knowledge_graph, knowledge_graph_api, llm_router, local_knowledge_api, telegram_bot, codex_telegram_bot, mcp_registry, p_reinforce, auto_setup) plus a top-level package literally named `tools` (line 79) — `tools` is a near-guaranteed clash with other PyPI packages and user code. Additionally [tool.setuptools.data-files] (lines 103-117) installs `static/` and `plugins/` directories into the interpreter prefix root — a deprecated setuptools mechanism that scatters app assets outside the package. Everything should live under the latticeai package for v4, with assets accessed via importlib.resources.

problems.title: Working tree is a 2.9GB junk drawer: 31 release tarballs, two venvs, extracted release dir, logs, secrets file
problems.detail: On-disk (all untracked/ignored, verified via git ls-files — 440 tracked files, 0 .tgz tracked): 31 ltcai-*.tgz tarballs (0.2.2 through 3.6.0, ~3-25MB each, roughly 300MB total) at repo root; ltcai-0.3.1/ extracted sdist (scripts/check_python.py line 52 even special-cases it in EXCLUDE_DIRS); venv/ (966MB) AND .venv/ (1.2GB) both inside the repo; dist/ containing stale 3.3.0-3.5.0 artifacts alongside 3.6.0 (exactly the stale-mixing the validator warns about); server.log, ai_server.log, chat_history.json, telegram_chats.json, .env (live Telegram/Discord bot tokens + permission secret), agent_workspace/ with demo apps, node_modules, .npm-cache, .build-venv, playwright-report, test-results. Also `git count-objects` reports garbage tmp_obj_* files in .git/objects from interrupted operations. None of this blocks git, but it makes the repo state illegible, slows every rglob-based script, and risks accidental inclusion the moment an ignore rule is loosened.

problems.title: 15MB lattice_ai_full_spec.pptx tracked in git at HEAD and in history
problems.detail: lattice_ai_full_spec.pptx (15,345,134 bytes) is tracked (git ls-files confirms) and was committed in 7fc01a6 ('Release 0.3.1'). It bloats every clone forever even if deleted now; removal requires history rewrite (git filter-repo) or acceptance of the cost. docs/assets/v3.4.0/ and docs/images/ add dozens more binary screenshots/GIFs (hero.gif, lattice-ai-demo.gif) tracked in git. For a v4 reset, binaries belong in releases/LFS/external storage.

problems.title: Zero dependency pinning: no version constraints, no lockfile for Python
problems.detail: pyproject.toml dependencies (lines 30-47) and requirements.txt are two hand-duplicated, completely unpinned lists (`fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `cryptography`, ... with no constraints at all). There is no pip-tools/uv lock. A 'local-first, user owns their data' platform whose install resolves different dependency versions every day is not reproducible, and a breaking fastapi/pydantic major release will break every fresh install with no code change. requirements.txt and pyproject are currently in sync but have no mechanism keeping them so.

problems.title: npm package is a 24.8MB tarball shipping docs screenshots, Telegram bots, and a whole Python app
problems.detail: package.json `files` (lines 61-105) whitelists `docs/` wholesale, so ltcai-3.6.0.tgz (24.8MB, 313 files) ships 39 image files under docs/images + docs/assets (including multi-MB GIFs) plus telegram_bot.py, codex_telegram_bot.py and p_reinforce.py — visible in `tar -tzf`. Tarball size jumped from 13.8MB (3.1.0) to 23.5MB (3.4.0) exactly when screenshots were added. The npm channel itself is a shim (bin/ltcai.js) that bootstraps a Python venv in ~/.ltcai/npm-python — the same product is triple-published (npm + PyPI + VSIX), tripling release surface for v4 to maintain.

problems.title: Release-notes sprawl: 9+ overlapping release documents, two changelogs
problems.detail: Repo root carries RELEASE.md (797 lines — accumulated Korean release notes for every version since 0.4.0 plus the actual release runbook buried at line ~700), RELEASE_NOTES.md, RELEASE_NOTES_v3.3.0/v3.4.0/v3.4.1/v3.5.0/v3.6.0.md, CHANGELOG.md AND docs/CHANGELOG.md (root one delegates to docs but both restate 3.6.0), plus PLATFORM_COMPLETION_REPORT_v3.4.0.md and VISUAL_REBUILD_NOTES_v3.3.1.md. The root directory has ~20 markdown files. One CHANGELOG.md + docs/releases/vX.Y.Z.md (or GitHub Releases) would replace all of it.

problems.title: Dead and stale tracked files: perm_monitor.py, scripts/release-0.3.1.sh, committed build outputs
problems.detail: perm_monitor.py is tracked in git but imported by nothing (grep over all first-party Python finds zero importers) and excluded from both wheel py-modules and npm files — pure dead weight. scripts/release-0.3.1.sh is a one-off for a release 30 versions ago. static/v3/ commits BOTH hashed and unhashed copies of every CSS/JS asset (e.g. app.js + app.c541f955.js, ~40 duplicate pairs) — generated output of scripts/build_v3_assets.mjs checked into git, guaranteeing diff churn every release. tests/visual/v223-v227.spec.js are version-named specs accumulating per release.

problems.title: Version 'single source' is actually 9 synchronized copies held together by a test
problems.detail: The canonical version lives in latticeai/core/workspace_os.py (WORKSPACE_OS_VERSION) and must be manually kept equal in latticeai/__init__.py, pyproject.toml, package.json, package-lock.json, vscode-extension/package.json + its lockfile, static/v3/asset-manifest.json, MARKETPLACE_VERSION and MULTI_AGENT_VERSION. tests/unit/test_version_consistency.py makes drift fail loudly (good), but every release bump touches 9+ files. A real single source (importlib.metadata at runtime + a bump script writing the two package.json files) would shrink this.

problems.title: No dependabot/renovate, no workflow concurrency control, no pytest config
problems.detail: .github/ has CODEOWNERS, issue templates, PR template and 3 workflows but no dependabot.yml — with fully unpinned deps there is also no automated update signal. Workflows lack `concurrency` groups (parallel pushes run redundant full matrices). There is no [tool.pytest.ini_options] anywhere — no testpaths, no asyncio_mode — so pytest behavior depends on whatever plugins happen to be installed; the documented invocation (.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit) lives only in tribal knowledge/AGENTS.md.

opportunities.title: Add an installed-wheel smoke test to CI and release workflows
opportunities.detail: After `python -m build`, create a clean venv, `pip install dist/ltcai-X.Y.Z-py3-none-any.whl`, then `python -c "import server; assert server.app"` and hit /health via uvicorn — from a non-repo cwd so repo-root modules can't mask packaging omissions. This single job would have caught the broken v3.6.0 wheel (missing `setup` module) and will catch any future py-modules/package-data drift. Wire it into ci.yml build job and release.yml before validate_release_artifacts.py.

opportunities.title: Repackage everything under the latticeai namespace for v4
opportunities.detail: Move the 12 root legacy modules (knowledge_graph.py, kg_schema.py, llm_router.py, setup.py->setup_wizard.py, telegram_bot.py, etc.) and the top-level `tools` package into latticeai/ (keep thin root shims only for the dev tree if needed); move static/ and plugins/ into latticeai/static + latticeai/plugins served via importlib.resources; delete [tool.setuptools.data-files] and the py-modules list entirely. This fixes the setup.py collision, the broken wheel, and the site-packages namespace pollution in one structural move, and is the packaging foundation the Digital Brain Platform needs to be pip-installable as a durable local app.

opportunities.title: Adopt ruff + mypy + ESLint with CI gates
opportunities.detail: Add [tool.ruff] (lint+format) and [tool.mypy] (start permissive, strict on latticeai/services and latticeai/core where the knowledge/memory/provenance logic lives — the durable-knowledge code paths deserve type safety most), plus ESLint flat config for static/v3/js and static/scripts. Replace the node --check chain in package.json and scripts/lint_v3.mjs with eslint, keep check_python.py as the fast syntax gate, and add both to ci.yml. Add [tool.pytest.ini_options] with testpaths and asyncio_mode.

opportunities.title: Pin dependencies with a lock file and delete requirements.txt duplication
opportunities.detail: Adopt uv (or pip-tools): keep loose-but-bounded constraints in pyproject (e.g. fastapi>=0.110,<1), generate a committed lock for the supported Python versions, and make CI/release install from the lock. A privacy-first local platform must produce the same install next year that it produces today — 'models are temporary, knowledge is durable' applies to the runtime too. Delete requirements.txt or generate it from pyproject.

opportunities.title: v4 repo reset: purge clutter from disk and history
opportunities.detail: Delete from disk: all 31 ltcai-*.tgz, ltcai-0.3.1/, stale dist/ artifacts, venv/, server.log/ai_server.log, .git tmp objects (git gc). Rewrite history (or accept and stop the bleeding) for lattice_ai_full_spec.pptx; move docs/images and docs/assets screenshots to GitHub Release assets or LFS. Consolidate the 9 release documents into CHANGELOG.md + docs/releases/. Remove dead perm_monitor.py and scripts/release-0.3.1.sh. Stop committing hashed static/v3 build outputs — build them in CI (build_v3_assets.mjs already exists) and assert via the existing asset-manifest test. Target: a repo root with <10 files where every tracked file is load-bearing.

opportunities.title: Pick one primary distribution channel for v4 and automate publish from the tag
opportunities.detail: Decide whether the Digital Brain Platform's install story is PyPI (pipx install ltcai), npm shim, or a packaged app — maintaining npm+PyPI+VSIX+OpenVSX with manual local `publish:all` scripts is 4x release surface. Keep the excellent no-auto-publish stance but move publishing into a manually-approved GitHub Environment job in release.yml (uses the already-validated artifacts, exact filenames, OIDC trusted publishing for PyPI) so releases stop depending on one developer's laptop having twine/vsce/npm credentials. Trim the npm files whitelist (exclude docs/, telegram bots) if npm is kept.

opportunities.title: Generate the 9-file version bump from one source
opportunities.detail: Add scripts/bump_version.py that takes X.Y.Z and rewrites workspace_os.py, latticeai/__init__.py, pyproject.toml, both package.json+lockfiles, vscode-extension, and regenerates asset-manifest — keeping test_version_consistency.py as the guard. Pairs with the existing release-manager flow; eliminates the most error-prone manual step of every release.

opportunities.title: Keep and extend the release validator
opportunities.detail: validate_release_artifacts.py, build_vsix.mjs, check_python.py, test_version_consistency.py, and the three workflows are the strongest engineering in this dimension — keep all of them for v4. Extend the validator with: wheel content assertions (required top-level modules/packages present, no unexpected files), a max-size budget per artifact (would have flagged the 24.8MB npm tarball), and a check that the sdist builds into an importable wheel.
